chunks: And I am certainly not one to drive away the believers.

key_terms.طَارِدِ: one who drives away or expels

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean when he says 'I am not one to drive away the believers' in Surah Ash-Shu'ara?
ai.summary: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara (26:222), this verse serves as a divine reassurance to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not responsible for expelling believers from Paradise, emphasizing the distinction between his role as a warner and God's role as the ultimate judge. Shia exegesis highlights this as a key attribute of the Prophet's humility and patience, reinforcing that his duty was to convey the message clearly without coercing belief or forcing adherence. This underscores the theological principle of 'no compulsion in religion' and the Prophet's gentle approach to guiding the Ummah.
